repairs.failure_pattern: Binary ROC-AUC computation fails with "continuous format is not supported" after MixUp or CutMix produces fractional training targets.
repair_steps: Retain the original binary labels before applying MixUp or CutMix.
Use the mixed soft labels only when computing the training loss.
Compute training ROC-AUC against original binary labels, or omit training AUC for mixed batches.
Continue computing validation ROC-AUC on an augmentation-free loader with untouched binary labels.
repairs.root_cause: MixUp and CutMix create soft labels for loss computation, but binary ROC-AUC requires ground-truth targets from the discrete classes.
repairs.title: Confirmed: Preserve binary targets separately from MixUp/CutMix loss targets
repairs.when_to_use: Use when a binary image classifier applies label-mixing augmentation and metric evaluation receives fractional targets or raises a continuous-target error.

repairs.failure_pattern: Binary classifier initialization fails because BCEWithLogitsLoss rejects a label_smoothing keyword.
repair_steps: Initialize BCEWithLogitsLoss only with arguments supported by the installed runtime, preserving any required class weighting such as pos_weight.
If smoothing is necessary, transform binary targets before loss evaluation using y_smooth = y * (1 - epsilon) + 0.5 * epsilon.
Keep original unsmoothed binary targets for ROC-AUC and other classification metrics.
Otherwise remove label smoothing and use ordinary BCEWithLogitsLoss.
repairs.root_cause: The binary BCE-with-logits loss API in the installed PyTorch version does not implement the label_smoothing option used by the pipeline.
repairs.title: Confirmed: Implement binary label smoothing outside BCEWithLogitsLoss
repairs.when_to_use: Use when training a binary image classifier and BCEWithLogitsLoss raises an unexpected-keyword TypeError for label_smoothing.

repairs.failure_pattern: A shared feature-extraction routine fails on test data by unpacking the wrong number of batch fields or treating image identifiers as tensor labels.
repair_steps: Define explicit dataset contracts for labeled batches such as (images, labels, ids) and unlabeled batches such as (images, ids).
Pass an explicit labeled or unlabeled mode to the extraction routine, or branch on a validated batch schema.
Convert labels to arrays only for labeled batches and collect identifiers as strings for both schemas.
Return a consistent result structure with features, optional labels, and ordered identifiers.
Assert that extracted feature rows, optional label rows, and identifier counts agree before caching or inference.
repairs.root_cause: Training and validation datasets emit image-label-ID batches while the unlabeled test dataset emits image-ID batches, but the extraction routine assumes one fixed schema.
repairs.title: Confirmed: Normalize labeled and unlabeled DataLoader batch schemas during feature extraction
repairs.when_to_use: Use when one frozen vision feature extractor serves train, validation, and unlabeled test loaders whose dataset outputs have different tuple structures.

repairs.failure_pattern: Cross-validation ensemble inference completes, but submission creation fails because the number or order of test identifiers does not match the averaged test predictions.
repair_steps: Use a deterministic test loader with shuffling disabled.
During one complete inference pass, append every batch's identifiers to a flat ordered list alongside its prediction vector.
For later folds, reuse the established identifier order and verify that each fold emits the same ordered identifiers.
Average fold predictions only after asserting identical prediction shapes across folds.
Before creating the submission, assert that identifier count equals prediction count and equals the test dataset size.
repairs.root_cause: Test identifiers are incompletely accumulated, overwritten between batches or folds, or collected independently from the prediction order.
repairs.title: Provisional: Build submission identifiers from the same ordered inference stream as predictions
repairs.when_to_use: Use when producing an ensemble submission and test IDs are gathered inside batch or fold loops, especially after a length mismatch at DataFrame construction.

repairs.failure_pattern: A custom CNN reaches its classifier but fails matrix multiplication because flattened convolutional features do not match the first linear layer's declared input width.
repair_steps: Run a representative image tensor through the convolutional feature stack before training and inspect the resulting shape.
Set the first linear layer's input width to the product of the actual non-batch feature dimensions.
Prefer adaptive pooling to a fixed spatial size when input resolution or convolutional geometry may vary.
Add a model smoke test that performs one forward pass and asserts an output shape of one logit per image.
repairs.root_cause: The classifier input dimension was calculated from an incorrect channel count or spatial resolution after pooling.
repairs.title: Provisional: Derive CNN classifier input width from the actual feature tensor
repairs.when_to_use: Use when a from-scratch CNN for fixed-size cactus images reports incompatible matrix shapes at the convolutional-to-linear boundary.

repairs.failure_pattern: Training and checkpoint saving succeed, but loading the best checkpoint for test inference raises a weights-only unpickling error under newer PyTorch behavior.
repair_steps: Save the model state_dict and primitive metadata instead of serializing the complete model object.
Recreate the model architecture in code before loading the checkpoint.
Load the state dictionary with the runtime's explicit weights-only mode and then call model.load_state_dict.
Use unrestricted deserialization only for a trusted legacy checkpoint that cannot be converted, and specify that behavior explicitly.
Perform a checkpoint reload smoke test immediately after saving, before the full training run proceeds to final inference.
repairs.root_cause: The pipeline saves a general Python checkpoint object while loading it through a runtime whose torch.load defaults to restricted weights-only deserialization.
repairs.title: Provisional: Save and reload model state dictionaries with an explicit checkpoint contract
repairs.when_to_use: Use when a best-model checkpoint saved during binary image training cannot be reloaded because of PyTorch weights-only deserialization behavior.
